admission.justification: Both the per-harness copies and a read-with-fallback were weighed and rejected, and every harness installation now depends on the one shared path.

alternatives.option: One shared <coordinationRoot>/system/settings.json block is the authority: starter/setup creates it once, each harness links the coordination root and reads that same file per use, and no per-harness copy of the block exists.
alternatives.reason: One installation has one host, so one place states it; reading per use means a block added after a server started is used without a restart, and the setup still gives every harness a file it can start from.

alternatives.option: Keep a full block per harness, kept in sync by the setup.
alternatives.reason: Eight copies of one fact drift, and an agent can be started by a harness whose file names another host.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Harnesses stop sharing one coordination root, so no installation-wide path exists.

alternatives.option: Read the shared block first and fall back to a per-harness block when it is absent.
alternatives.reason: A fallback keeps the old independent copies alive and hides which authority a running host was started from; the migration is instead an explicit instruction that the developer runs when they choose.
alternatives.reconsider_when: An installation cannot share one filesystem authority and a migration proves impossible.

consequences: The old per-harness block is ignored with one warning naming the shared path and the exact migration, with no fallback.
The developer owns the real settings edit and the host restart that follows it.
context: Eight settings files of one machine named the same coordination root and could each hold a different paseoRuntime block; only the Codex file held one, and a dashboard started without --config read a file that held none. The developer has called a setting copied into every harness's file a nuisance (D63).
decider: ruling OR-R034 under D63 and D75
